summary: Code review PASS. dialogue_writer.py is clean, well-structured stdlib-only code. Module placement, SRP decomposition, defensive error handling, and Markdown serialisation logic are all correct and idiomatic. All 39 tests pass. No blocking issues, no fix-forwards needed.

comments.note: No blocking issues. Module placement in src/utils/ is correct for a stateless I/O utility. Single-responsibility decomposition (_msg_role, _render_content, _render_tool_calls, _collect_usage → serialize_messages_to_markdown → write_dialogue) is clean and easy to reason about.

_render_content's list-branch filters empty-string parts via `if p`. This is correct Markdown behaviour and will not silently drop meaningful content in practice, but it is worth noting as a subtle invariant: empty string parts from content blocks are intentionally discarded.

write_dialogue() iterates all existing files and uses max() rather than trusting lexicographic sort order — this is the correct and more robust approach (handles non-contiguous revision numbers gracefully). Well done.

The _render_content() function handles Anthropic/OpenAI list-of-content-blocks format (dicts with 'type' key). This is undocumented LangChain API surface knowledge embedded in the implementation. The Documentation agent should add a brief inline comment or docstring noting what providers emit this format and why the 'text' block type is singled out — future maintainers will benefit from the context.

The System message role is handled in _msg_role() but has no dedicated test class (noted by QA). This is a low-priority gap that does not affect any acceptance criterion. The Documentation agent may wish to note in the module docstring that System messages are supported.
